Definition: from G1537 and the base of G1416; to cause to sink out of, i.e. (specially as of clothing) to divest:--strip, take off from, unclothe.
BiblicalUsage: To strip off is to take clothing away, and the Gospels use it for Jesus and for the man on the Jericho road. The soldiers strip Jesus and put a scarlet robe on Him, then take the robe off and put His own clothes back on Him to lead Him to the cross, and the thieves strip the traveller, wound him, and leave him half dead. The word is shame and robbery in both stories, and one ends in a cross while the other ends in a Samaritan's mercy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus was stripped so that I could be clothed, because He bore the shame of nakedness that I might be covered in His righteousness. I hold that the good Samaritan's mercy is the picture of what Christ did for me on the road.
